espn-604005.headline: England are handed the bill for Cardiff
beats: New Zealand lost 35–28 to Wales on Saturday, their first defeat by Wales in 73 years. Eddie Jones has warned England to expect a "violent" response, and England say they are braced for one.

England come in on four straight wins, the last a 78–15 rout of Japan in which Will Joseph scored five tries on his second cap. New Zealand have now conceded 43 to South Africa and 35 to Wales in their two defeats since September.
Beat England by 16 or more and New Zealand go back to first in the world. England last lost by that much in July, 45–21 in South Africa.
England also beat New Zealand 33–19 at home last November. Ollie Chessum, the vice-captain, is back from a shoulder injury. New Zealand have had a week to think about Cardiff.

espn-604006.headline: Townsend rehearses for next year; Japan just let in 78
beats: Gregor Townsend plans changes to simulate scenarios his side might face at next year's World Cup. One could be Josh McKay, the 29-year-old New Zealand-born Glasgow full-back who qualified on residency five years after arriving at Scotstoun, with 25 tries in 85 games for the club.
Japan look like a convenient opponent for a rehearsal. They lost to Wales by seven on 7 November. A week later England put 78 on them.

Scotland have just won ugly, 15–12 over Australia in the wet. Townsend rated it one of his side's best defensive performances in recent years. Lose here by any margin and Scotland drop below that same Australia in the rankings.
Scotland's next Test is Italy in February. Japan have nothing scheduled after Murrayfield, which makes it a rehearsal for only one of them.

espn-604007.headline: Beaten in Paris, South Africa bring first place to Dublin
beats: South Africa left the Aviva 24–13 winners a year ago. They come back ranked first in the world, but France beat them 21–19 in their last game. An Ireland win drops them to second, below New Zealand.

Ireland arrive on bonus-point wins over Argentina and Fiji, 42–12 and 43–15, with seven tries in the second. Dan Sheehan has been cleared to captain them after the concussion that kept him out against Fiji.

Rassie Erasmus has made five changes, with Eben Etzebeth back in the starting XV. He also says Sam Prendergast's cited hip-drop tackle on Fiji captain Peceli Yato deserved a red card. He expects it not to matter: "I think there is going to be a technicality and he is going to play."
If he is right, South Africa defend first place against the out-half their coach wanted punished.

espn-604008.headline: One of them stops losing. Italy's press doubts it's them
beats: Italy and Fiji have each lost all five of their Nations Championship games so far. Italy are 11th, Fiji 12th, split by one table point and three points of difference.
Italy had a storming first half hour against Argentina in Genoa and still lost 14–19, their sixth straight defeat. One Italian headline afterwards: "L'Italia non sa più vincere".
Fiji have conceded 54 and 43 in a fortnight, away to France and Ireland. A win in Udine lifts Italy above them to ninth in the world rankings.
Italy are already fixed as North 6th, so their final-weekend game at Twickenham is against the South's bottom side. That could well be Fiji again, which gives the loser a second go within days.

espn-604009.headline: France top the North by one point and one header
beats: France beat South Africa 21–19, and the game turned partly on a lucky try that came from an accidental header by Kalvin Gourgues. That leaves them first in the North with one pool game left, a point clear of England.
Argentina's margins have been thin too. They lost 42–12 in Ireland, then scraped past Italy 19–14 in Genoa in a game of indiscipline and loose handling, with Italy still able to win it late.
France have recalled Matthieu Jalibert to the 42-man squad to ease an injury crisis. He tore his right quadriceps on 20 September, relapsed in mid-October and has not played for nearly two months.
Lose this, and France drop to fifth in the world, below England. That is the same side they are trying to keep behind them in the table.

espn-604010.headline: Ticket sales up 700%, and Australia have lost four
beats: Wales beat New Zealand 35–28 in Cardiff on 14 November, their first win over them since 1953. In the buildup, one New Zealand newspaper had likened them to “Dickensian orphans”.
Eddie James, 24, made 25 tackles that day and said afterwards he could not feel his feet. Steve Tandy has told his side the job now is to back it up.

Australia's autumn has gone the other way: 50 and 43 conceded to New Zealand in October, 45 to England, then a 15–12 defeat at Murrayfield in an attritional game Scotland's coach praised for its defence. They have not scored more than 22 in any of those four losses.
Win, and Wales go up to ninth in the world, with Australia down to eighth. The people who bought those tickets on the strength of one result will expect a second.
